evidence: Ran python3 -I test_state_contract.py at commit a8000d33: 24/24 tests passed (exit 0). Built a pinned state-contract schema (8 kinds) plus validator for state/operator-system/** (operator_system_pointer, instruction_stack, authority_envelope, commission, function, appointment, runtime_binding, alias). Each kind's required_fields (key intersection) and allowed_status_values (observed status union) were derived programmatically from the 20 real committed records and pinned as CONTRACT; TestContractMatchesRepoSnapshot independently re-derives the same values live and asserts an exact match, proving the pin is grounded not invented. Real-repo run (real_repo_run.json) shows all 20 records across 8 kinds validate cleanly (all_valid=true, total_errors=0). The core hypothesis was tested directly: for every one of the 8 kinds, a deep-copy of the actual currently-valid real record with only its status field set to a synthetic never-committed value (UNDEFINED_STATE_NEVER_COMMITTED_ANYWHERE) was rejected by validate_record with exactly one precise named error, while the untouched original still validates -- demonstrating undefined states cannot silently pass. A byte-comparison test confirms none of the 8 real source files were mutated by any validation call in the suite.
falsifiable_hypothesis: The operator state vocabulary can be expressed as an enforceable contract so undefined states cannot enter committed state files.
limitations: Contract enforces only required-field presence and status-vocabulary membership per kind (open-world on other fields, matching this repo's own additive-only migration doctrine); it does not constrain the separate, already-enforced obzio_state/RESULT_STATES vocabulary in workstreams/po03/tools/validate_contracts.py, which is a distinct transactional-result-protocol vocabulary outside this unit's operator-system scope. The pin is a point-in-time snapshot of state/operator-system/** and would need explicit review to admit any future legitimately-new status value.
